title: Probability as a finitely additive measure
dek: A probability is a number on events that is nonnegative, normalised, and additive on disjoint pieces. Everything later — likelihoods, p-values, posteriors — is a reading of this object, not a replacement for it.
story: Before a sampling model or a posterior, there is a sample space Ω of outcomes you are willing to treat as the universe of the experiment, a collection of events (subsets of Ω) you will assign numbers to, and a function P that sends those events to [0, 1]. Kolmogorov’s three working rules are: P(A) ≥ 0; P(Ω) = 1; and if A and B are disjoint, P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B). Countable additivity is the same sentence with a countable disjoint union.

Those rules are not a theory of belief and they are not a theory of long-run frequency. They are the grammar both cultures speak. A p-value is P(discrepancy as large as observed | H₀). A posterior is P(θ in a set | data). A diagnostic predictive value is P(disease | test+). If two numbers refuse to add on a partition, at least one of them is not a probability in this sense.

In a TB lab the sample space is a modelling choice: isolates in a survey, reads at a site, households in a cluster. Changing Ω changes every probability downstream. “The probability of rifampin resistance” without saying among whom, in which year, under which sampling rule, is a slogan, not an event.
deep: Complement: P(Aᶜ) = 1 − P(A). This is why a test with sensitivity 0.90 still has a 10% false-negative rate among the diseased — that 0.10 is P(T− | D+), not a property of the whole waiting room.
Inclusion–exclusion for two events: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B). Adding two overlapping prevalences as if they were disjoint is how comorbidity slides exceed 100%.
Monotonicity: A ⊂ B implies P(A) ≤ P(B). A 12-SNP transmission window cannot be more probable than a 5-SNP window on the same data and the same model unless you changed the event.

Conditional probability is not a fourth axiom. It is a derived construction: P(A | B) := P(A ∩ B)/P(B) when P(B) > 0. Independence is the special case P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B). Both live on later plates; they are not extra axioms.

A density or mass function is a way of specifying P, not a different kind of number. Discrete: P(Y = y) = f(y). Continuous: P(Y ∈ A) = ∫_A f. The axioms constrain the integral or the sum, which is why a “probability” of 1.3 on a pie chart is not a rounding error — it is a broken measure.

formulas.label: Working axioms
formulas.note: Countable additivity replaces the last line with a countable disjoint union.

formulas.label: Two-event inclusion–exclusion
formulas.expression: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A ∩ B)
formulas.note: The intersection is subtracted once because it was counted twice.

visual.caption: From a named sample space to a number on an event. Disjoint pieces add. Overlapping pieces do not. Conditional probability is a later reweighting, not a fourth axiom.

example.title: Two overlapping resistance events
example.setup: In a survey of 200 RR-TB isolates, 40 are FQ-R (event F) and 24 are BDQ-R by catalogue (event B). 10 isolates are both. Someone adds 40/200 + 24/200 and reports a 32% “Group A problem” rate.

steps.title: Name the events
steps.body: F = FQ-R, B = BDQ-R. They are not disjoint: 10 isolates sit in F ∩ B. Adding P̂(F) + P̂(B) counts those ten twice.

steps.title: Check the axioms
steps.body: 0.27 is in [0, 1] and is smaller than P̂(F) + P̂(B) = 0.32, as monotonicity and inclusion–exclusion require. The 32% figure is not a probability of a union.

steps.title: What the union still is not
steps.body: P(F ∪ B) is not pre-XDR prevalence (that needs FQ among MDR/RR) and is not 2021-XDR (that needs FQ plus BDQ or LZD). The axiom only stopped the double count. The WHO definition is a different event.

example.takeaway: Additivity is licensed on a partition. Overlap is subtracted, not wished away.

check.prompt: P(A ∪ B) = P(A) + P(B) is guaranteed when:
choices: A and B are any two events in Ω
A and B are disjoint (cannot occur together)
check.answer: A and B are disjoint (cannot occur together)
check.why: Additivity is an axiom for disjoint events. Independence is a different relation and does not make the intersection empty.

whyWrong.A and B are any two events in Ω: Then you must subtract P(A ∩ B).
whyWrong.n > 30: Sample size is not an axiom.
whyWrong.A and B are independent: Independent events can still overlap; P(A ∩ B) = P(A)P(B) can be positive.

whyWrong.0.65: That adds without subtracting the overlap.
whyWrong.0.10: That is the intersection, not the union.
whyWrong.0.75: That would require a negative intersection.

check.prompt: On the flow plate, why does overlap take a different path from disjoint additivity?
check.figureHint: Two decision nodes after Event A.
choices: Because overlapping events are not allowed in Kolmogorov’s axioms
Because overlapping pieces were counted twice if you add, so the intersection must be subtracted to get a number in [0,1] that matches the union
Because conditional probability is a fourth axiom
check.answer: Because overlapping pieces were counted twice if you add, so the intersection must be subtracted to get a number in [0,1] that matches the union
check.why: The axioms do not forbid overlap. They forbid treating overlap as a partition.

whyWrong.Because overlapping events are not allow: They are allowed; inclusion–exclusion handles them.
whyWrong.Because conditional probability is a fou: Conditional probability is derived, not axiomatic.
